title: Open WebUI terminal proxy -- T1027 9x percent-encoding survives an 8-round decode cap and reaches a traversal path
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59221 (GHSA-frvj-c5qp-xj4w,
CVSS 7.7 HIGH -- corrected 2026-09-04 via live GHSA lookup, the rule's
original authoring understated this score), an incomplete fix for the
earlier GHSA-r2wg-2mcr-66rv terminal proxy traversal, present in Open
WebUI v0.9.6 and prior main.

`_sanitize_proxy_path()` in `backend/open_webui/routers/terminals.py`
decodes a caller-supplied path parameter for up to 8 `unquote()`
rounds, then applies `posixpath.normpath()` and a `..`-prefix check to
the result. A path parameter encoded 9 times still contains one layer
of percent-encoded dot/slash bytes after those 8 rounds, so the
traversal check runs against literal `%2E%2E%2F...` text rather than
`../...` and passes. The sanitized-but-still-encoded value is
forwarded to the configured terminal server, which decodes it itself
and turns it back into a traversal (`/base/../admin/system`) --
reaching upstream paths outside the intended normalized proxy path
with the connection's forwarded credentials and `X-User-Id` header.

Detection logic flags a terminal-proxy path parameter carrying 9 or
more literal `%25` sequences (the escaped-`%` signature of a
multiply-encoded payload surviving into the request) -- the exact
over-encoding depth this advisory's fixed 8-round decode cap fails to
unwind.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact function, source file, and a
reproduction script demonstrating the 8-vs-9-round boundary), fixed in
Open WebUI 0.10.0+ (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the
rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this
note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
